### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/report.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/report.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/report.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/report.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53749673ba7a0005d09e8a79544da10d5faa10bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `847bfd6e2f3d34bbd48063b470dada58e9b31cef` — the merge of head `39eb423b391b593f8cd4d981f126ca60af308758` into base `53749673ba7a0005d09e8a79544da10d5faa10bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 847bfd6e2f3d34bbd48063b470dada58e9b31cef && git checkout 847bfd6e2f3d34bbd48063b470dada58e9b31cef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53749673ba7a0005d09e8a79544da10d5faa10bc 39eb423b391b593f8cd4d981f126ca60af308758 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53749673ba7a0005d09e8a79544da10d5faa10bc && git merge --no-ff 39eb423b391b593f8cd4d981f126ca60af308758

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53749673ba7a0005d09e8a79544da10d5faa10bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); the one file `main` moved since the merge-base that is also in this diff, `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, merges without conflict.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The card's effect, as ordered** - right. `DatasetReportChart` reads `chart.seriesBy` as a string and, on a series plan, widens its own query to `[xAxis, seriesBy]` × `[yAxis]`; `buildChartSeries` is handed `queryDimensions`, so with a split it takes the pivot branch it already runs for a two-dimension dashboard widget (one row per x bucket, one column per split value, the null group under the translated `(None)`), and without one it takes the single-dimension branch it took before. Pinned: the query the source receives, the pivoted rows, the `xAxisKey`, and the CONTROL (no `seriesBy`: one `owner` query, one `total_amount` series labelled from the field, rows passed through). `chart-series.ts` is untouched.
- **Series order and labels** - right. The split joins `chartDimensions`, so the dimension-metadata read covers it and `relabel[1]` is the split; its localized options give `seriesOrder`, the pivoted series are sorted by `declaredOptionPosition` with the null label last, and the same `scopeOrder` opt-out the categories use applies (a report `order` that reaches the chart's selection keeps the server's order). With a split the measure's display name is stamped on no series; each keeps its (relabeled) value, and a `series[]` entry naming that value lands its presentation through `mergeAuthoredSeries` and its label through `pickLocalized`. The `authoredSeries[i]` / `derivedSeries[i]` pairing is safe because `mergeAuthoredSeries` maps the derived list in place.
- **The cross-domain edits are the triage exception and its S2 rider, plus prose the change made false** - right. `packages/spec/liveness/report.json`: `chart.children.seriesBy` planned to live with the renderer and the new test as evidence, `authorWarn` / `authorHint` dropped; the `chart` row's note drops its stale `groupBy` sentence (S2) and names the split. `state-counts/report.md` is the generated shard (live 39 to 40, planned 1 to 0, classified 41) that `check:liveness` requires after the flip. `packages/lint` changes are comment and `os explain` prose only: the header quote is re-synced to the renderer's new sentence, and no rule, severity or finding moves.
- **S1 stays with the spec lane, as triage ruled** - right. The body records the measured location (`packages/lint/src/validate-chart-bindings.ts`, `@objectstack/lint`, not `packages/spec`) for the hand-over.
- **Accept-set: nothing an author writes moves** - right. No spec schema changes; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold (no new export; the ui change is inside one component).
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@object-ui/plugin-report`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint` all patch; `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`** - accepted. The renderer changes behaviour only when a key that was declared-but-inert is present; the spec entry covers the published liveness ledger and the lint entry covers explanation text. Patch is the most either could be.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Two follow-ups for the spec lane, named in the body and not filed** - (a) rider S1, the `seriesBy === xAxis` warning in `validateChartBindings`; (b) a single-series family (`pie` / `donut` / `funnel`) with `seriesBy` now hands the chart several series, which draws the chart's single-series refusal notice where it drew one series before; the spec does not refuse the key on those types. Both are spec-lane decisions outside this card's surface. The seat routes them with S1.
- **`series[].name` matches the series key, which is the server-resolved display label, not the stored option value** - noted in the body; it is the same rule `mergeAuthoredSeries` applies everywhere, so not a defect of this diff.
- **No name approval owed** - the key was ruled with #27974 and PR #28191.

**Verdict reasoning.** The diff draws the key where the card said, by handing the existing pivot both dimensions rather than re-deriving a split; order and labels follow the derivations the dashboard widget already uses; a chart without the key is byte-for-byte what it was, pinned by the CONTROL and an ablation shown three red / one green. The ledger flip and its generated shard are the triage exception; the lint edits are prose. Semver is patch everywhere. The two open questions are spec-lane follow-ups the body names.
